messages.content: You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
Inertia is the tendency of an object to keep doing what it is already doing, whether that’s staying still or moving at a constant speed.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
Actually, inertia keeps the car moving; it’s friction and brakes that bring it to a halt.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
No, inertia is about resisting changes in motion, while gravity pulls objects toward each other.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
Inertia actually means the opposite: an object resists changes in its speed, so it stays at rest or moves uniformly unless acted upon by an external force.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
It’s the property that keeps a stationary object from moving until a force acts on it, and keeps a moving object traveling at constant velocity unless a force changes that motion.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
The skateboard’s inertia keeps it moving, but friction is the force that eventually slows it down.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
They’re related: inertia is the resistance to change in motion, while momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
Actually, inertia keeps objects moving; it’s the external force that makes them stop.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
It’s the property that causes a body to maintain its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
The ball’s inertia keeps it rolling; friction is what brings it to rest.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
No, force is what changes motion, while inertia is the resistance to that change.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
That’s almost right: inertia keeps objects moving unless a force acts, but it also keeps them at rest if no force is applied.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
It’s the quality that makes a mass resist any change in its motion, whether that’s starting, stopping, or changing direction.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
The car’s inertia keeps it moving; the brakes apply a force that opposes that motion, causing it to slow down.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
Inertia itself doesn’t cause acceleration; it’s the resistance that needs a force to produce acceleration.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
What is inertia?
Inertia does keep objects at rest, but it also keeps moving objects traveling at constant speed unless a force changes that.
